options_english: At least once in a year
At least once every month
At least once in three years

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 213(1) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, the physical verification of fixed assets (recorded in Form GFR-22) must be conducted at least once in a year. The verification officer or committee must physically inspect each asset to confirm its existence, condition, and location, and subsequently record the verification certificate and remarks in the Register of Fixed Assets. Any discrepancy, shortage, or unserviceable condition identified during the annual verification must be promptly reported to the Head of Office / competent authority for investigation and administrative remedial action.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213(1) के अनुसार, सरकारी कार्यालय अथवा विद्यालय में सभी अचल परिसंपत्तियों (फॉर्म GFR-22 में दर्ज) का भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार (at least once in a year) अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाना चाहिए। सत्यापन अधिकारी अथवा समिति द्वारा परिसंपत्तियों की भौतिक उपस्थिति, कार्यदशा और स्थिति की जांच कर उसका प्रमाणपत्र रजिस्टर में दर्ज किया जाता है। यदि सत्यापन के दौरान कोई कमी, क्षति या अंतर पाया जाता है, तो उसे तत्काल सक्षम प्राधिकारी के संज्ञान में लाया जाना चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) At least once a year

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 213 of the General Financial Rules 2017 mandates that physical verification of fixed assets must be conducted at least once every year. The physical verification process verifies the physical existence and condition of assets, helps reconcile physical records with stock registers, and identifies missing, damaged, or unserviceable items requiring administrative action.

questions.question_english: Which of the following entities is NOT automatically governed by the provisions of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 unless expressly adopted?
options_english: Attached offices of a Central Ministry
Subordinate offices of a Central Ministry
Central Government Departments
State Government Departments
questions.explanation_english: The General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 are framed and issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, under executive powers for transactions relating to the Consolidated Fund of India and the Public Account of India. All Central Government Ministries, Departments, attached offices, and subordinate offices are automatically and statutorily bound by GFR 2017. Conversely, State Government departments are sovereign administrative units governed by their respective State Financial Codes and rules enacted pursuant to Articles 202-207 and 283 of the Constitution. Therefore, GFR 2017 does not automatically apply to State Government departments unless specifically adopted by an executive order of that State.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 केंद्र सरकार के वित्त मंत्रालय द्वारा जारी किए गए हैं और ये भारत की संचित निधि तथा लोक लेखा से संबंधित लेन-देन पर स्वतः लागू होते हैं। केंद्र सरकार के सभी मंत्रालय, विभाग, संलग्न कार्यालय और अधीनस्थ कार्यालय इससे अनिवार्य रूप से बंधे हैं। इसके विपरीत, राज्य सरकारों के अपने अलग वित्तीय नियम और संहिताएं (State Financial Codes) होती हैं। राज्य सरकार के विभाग केंद्रीय GFR से स्वतः बाध्य नहीं हैं, जब तक कि संबंधित राज्य सरकार औपचारिक अधिसूचना द्वारा इसे स्वीकार न कर ले।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) State Government Departments

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: State Government departments are governed by their respective state financial codes and rules framed under constitutional powers. Consequently, central General Financial Rules do not apply to state administrative units unless a state government explicitly decides to adopt them through formal notification. In contrast, all central departments, including their attached and subordinate offices, are automatically bound by the central financial rules framework.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The procuring authority must ensure fair, open, and equitable treatment of all eligible suppliers during the public procurement process.
Reason (R): Transparency and genuine competition are indispensable to achieve the best value for money in public procurement.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

1. Mandate under GFR Rule 144: Rule 144 of GFR 2017 establishes that procuring authorities must afford equal and non-discriminatory opportunity to all eligible bidders.
2. Economic Rationale: When government procurement is fair and transparent, more vendors participate without fear of bias or favoritism. Robust competition drives down commercial prices, enhances product quality, eliminates cartels, and ensures that the public exchequer attains the optimal "value for money". Hence, Reason (R) provides the foundational economic and policy rationale that explains why Assertion (A) is mandated.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या प्रस्तुत करता है।

1. GFR नियम 144 के तहत अधिदेश: GFR 2017 का नियम 144 यह स्थापित करता है कि खरीद प्राधिकारियों को सभी पात्र बोलीदाताओं को समान और गैर-भेदभावपूर्ण अवसर प्रदान करना चाहिए।
2. आर्थिक औचित्य: जब सरकारी खरीद निष्पक्ष और पारदर्शी होती है, तो आपूर्तिकर्ता बिना किसी पक्षपात के डर के बोली प्रक्रिया में भाग लेते हैं। मजबूत और स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा से कीमतें कम होती हैं, उत्पाद की गुणवत्ता में सुधार होता है और सरकार को सार्वजनिक धन का सर्वोत्तम मूल्य (Value for Money) प्राप्त होता है। इसलिए, कारण (R) यह सटीक तार्किक व्याख्या प्रदान करता है कि अभिकथन (A) क्यों अनिवार्य किया गया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Procuring authorities are required to offer fair and equitable treatment to all prospective suppliers throughout the public procurement process. Encouraging open competition and maintaining full transparency in bidding procedures prevents favoritism and allows the government to secure the best technical quality at the most economical market price, thereby achieving optimal value for expenditure of public money.

questions.question_english: Under which Rule of GFR 2017 has the Government of India made it mandatory for all Ministries and subordinate offices to procure common-use goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?

Rule 130
Rule 144

questions.explanation_english: Rule 149 of GFR 2017 specifically governs the 'Government e-Marketplace (GeM)'. The Ministry of Finance and the Government of India made procurement of common-use goods and services available on GeM mandatory for all Central Government Ministries, Departments, Subordinate/Attached offices, and Autonomous Bodies (including Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and Central Schools). The procuring authorities are required to verify the availability of items on GeM first, and only if an item is not available on GeM can offline procurement methods (Rules 154, 155, 161, 162) be resorted to, along with recording a Non-Availability Certificate (NAC) or justification.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 का नियम 149 विशेष रूप से 'गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस' (GeM) से संबंधित है। वित्त मंत्रालय के आदेशानुसार सभी केंद्रीय मंत्रालयों, विभागों, उनके अधीनस्थ कार्यालयों तथा स्वायत्त निकायों (जैसे केंद्रीय विद्यालय, नवोदय विद्यालय आदि) के लिए GeM पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की खरीद GeM पोर्टल के माध्यम से करना वैधानिक रूप से अनिवार्य है। किसी भी ऑफलाइन खरीद (नियम 154, 155, 161 आदि) को अपनाने से पहले क्रेता को GeM पर वस्तु की अनुपलब्धता (Non-Availability Certificate) सुनिश्चित करनी होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Rule 149

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules 2017 makes it mandatory for all central government ministries, departments, and subordinate offices to procure common-use goods and services through the online Government e-Marketplace (GeM). This statutory requirement aims to drive digital governance, consolidate government purchasing power, streamline administrative workflows, and eliminate manual procurement inefficiencies across public offices.

questions.question_english: Which of the following correctly describes a "Local Body" under the definitions of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017?
options_english: Only municipal corporations established in notified metropolitan cities.
Any authority legally entitled to, or entrusted by the Government with, the control or management of a local or municipal fund.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 2 of GFR 2017, a 'Local Body' is defined as an authority legally entitled to, or entrusted by the Government with, the control or management of a local or municipal fund. This broad statutory definition encompasses municipal corporations, municipalities, notified area committees, cantonment boards, zilla parishads, and gram panchayats. These bodies possess statutory powers to collect designated taxes/fees, receive grants-in-aid from the Government, and administer public funds for civic functions within their jurisdictional territories.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 2 के अनुसार, 'स्थानीय निकाय' (Local Body) से तात्पर्य ऐसे किसी भी प्राधिकारी से है जो सरकार द्वारा किसी स्थानीय या नगरपालिका निधि (Local or Municipal Fund) के नियंत्रण या प्रबंधन के लिए कानूनी रूप से अधिकृत अथवा सौंपा गया हो। इसमें नगर निगम, नगर पालिका परिषद, छावनी बोर्ड और पंचायती राज संस्थाएं सभी शामिल हैं। यह परिभाषा किसी गैर-सरकारी संगठन (NGO) पर लागू नहीं होती। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Any authority legally entitled to manage a local or municipal fund.

A local body is defined as any statutory or constitutional authority legally entrusted by government legislation with the administration and management of a dedicated local or municipal fund. This definition includes municipal corporations, town committees, district boards, and village panchayats. Such entities possess legal authority to levy local taxes, receive government grants, and execute public expenditure for local civic development.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 238 of GFR 2017, in respect of grants sanctioned for specific purposes or non-recurring capital expenditure, the grantee institution (such as a school) is legally required to submit a formal Utilization Certificate (UC) in the prescribed format (Form GFR 12-A / GFR 12-C). The UC serves as statutory accounting proof, certified by the Head of the Institution and audited by a Chartered Accountant or statutory auditor, confirming that the money was fully expended for the authorized purpose and that all stipulated sanction conditions were duly fulfilled.

questions.question_english: According to the Standards of Financial Propriety in GFR 2017, every public officer is required to exercise the same degree of vigilance in respect of public expenditure as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in respect of:
options_english: Corporate funds allocated to a publicly traded commercial company
Discretionary grants sanctioned to a registered philanthropic society
The expenditure of their own personal money
Trust property placed under their official legal guardianship
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 21(i) of GFR 2017, the very first canon of financial propriety stipulates:
"Every officer is expected to exercise the same vigilance in respect of expenditure incurred from public moneys as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in respect of expenditure of his own money."

Key implications for Educational Administrators / Principals:
1. Personal Care and Thrift: Public funds cannot be treated carelessly simply because they are state resources. An administrator must avoid unnecessary luxury, excessive quantities, and inflated pricing.
2. Duty of a DDO: As a Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO), a school Principal managing government budget grants, Samagra Shiksha funds, or student activity fees must ensure every rupee spent passes the test of ordinary personal prudence.
questions.explanation_hindi:

"प्रत्येक अधिकारी से यह अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वह सार्वजनिक धन से किए जाने वाले व्यय के संबंध में उतनी ही सतर्कता और विवेक बरतेगा, जितनी सामान्य विवेक वाला व्यक्ति अपने स्वयं के निजी धन के व्यय के संबंध में बरतता है।"

शैक्षिक प्रशासकों/प्राचार्यों के लिए मुख्य निहितार्थ:
1. व्यक्तिगत सतर्कता और मितव्ययिता: केवल इसलिए कि यह सरकारी धन है, इसे लापरवाही से खर्च नहीं किया जा सकता। एक प्रशासक को अनावश्यक विलासिता, आवश्यकता से अधिक मात्रा और अत्यधिक दरों से बचना चाहिए।
2. DDO का कर्तव्य: आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) के रूप में विद्यालय प्राचार्य को समग्र शिक्षा निधि, बजट अनुदान या छात्र कल्याण कोष खर्च करते समय यह सुनिश्चित करना होता है कि प्रत्येक रुपया उसी सावधानी से खर्च हो जैसे वह अपने निजी धन को खर्च करते।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) The expenditure of their own money

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The cardinal standard of financial propriety dictates that every government officer exercising financial powers must display the exact same degree of vigilance, prudence, and care over public expenditure as a person of ordinary prudence would naturally exercise when spending their own private money. Public funds must never be disbursed carelessly or utilized for extravagant, unnecessary, or unapproved personal and administrative purposes.

questions.question_english: Under GFR 2017, the procurement of services is broadly categorized into two types. What are they?
options_english: Consulting services and Non-consulting services
Domestic commercial services and International services
Primary administrative services and Secondary services
Direct operational services and Indirect services
questions.explanation_english:
Under Chapter 6 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, the procurement of services is bifurcated into two distinct categories:
1. Consulting Services (Rules 177 to 196): Covers assignments of an intellectual, technical, or advisory nature where specialized professional knowledge and expertise are procured (e.g., policy formulation, feasibility studies, engineering design, architectural consulting, legal counsel).
2. Non-Consulting Services (Rules 197 to 206): Covers physical, measurable, operational, or maintenance activities where measurable physical performance, labor, equipment, or materials predominate over specialized intellectual advice (e.g., security guard deployment, sanitation, catering, transportation, IT hardware maintenance).
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के अध्याय 6 के अंतर्गत सेवाओं की खरीद को दो प्रमुख श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया गया है:
1. परामर्श सेवाएं (Consulting Services - नियम 177 से 196): इसमें बौद्धिक, तकनीकी अथवा सलाहकारी प्रकृति के कार्य शामिल हैं जिनमें विशेष व्यावसायिक ज्ञान एवं विशेषज्ञता की आवश्यकता होती है (जैसे परियोजना अध्ययन, वास्तुशिल्प डिजाइन, कानूनी सलाह आदि)।
2. गैर-परामर्श सेवाएं (Non-Consulting Services - नियम 197 से 206): इसमें ऐसी भौतिक, परिचालन संबंधी अथवा नियमित रखरखाव वाली गतिविधियां शामिल हैं जिनमें श्रम, मशीनरी अथवा भौतिक प्रदर्शन की प्रधानता होती है और जिनके परिणामों को मापने योग्य इकाइयों में आंका जा सकता है (जैसे सुरक्षा सेवाएं, साफ-सफाई, खानपान, परिवहन सेवाएं आदि)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Consulting services and Non-consulting services

Non-consulting services involve physical, operational, or routine measurable activities where labor, equipment, or physical performance dominates over specialized professional advice.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT with regard to the operation of a 'Price Variation Clause' (PVC) in government procurement contracts under GFR 2017?
options_english: It provides for both upward and downward adjustments of contract prices linked to documented variations in recognized market indices.
It is typically included in long-duration procurement contracts where the delivery or execution period extends beyond 18 months.
The specific mathematical formula and permissible ceilings governing price variations must be unambiguously defined in the initial tender documents.
It empowers the contractor to unilaterally revise contract prices upward at their own discretion without presenting verified documentary evidence.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 225(viii) of GFR 2017 and procurement guidelines issued by the Department of Expenditure, a Price Variation Clause (PVC) is incorporated in long-term contracts (usually with an execution period exceeding 18 months) to account for market price fluctuations in raw materials, fuel, and statutory minimum wages. A valid PVC must always operate both ways (providing for price increases when indices rise and price deductions when indices drop), and the exact formula linked to recognized official price indices (like RBI indices or Wholesale Price Index) along with an upper ceiling must be clearly specified in the tender document. A contractor can NEVER unilaterally increase contract prices at their own whim without verifiable documentary proof and without following the contracted mathematical formula. Therefore, statement D is incorrect and is the right answer.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 225(viii) और व्यय विभाग के खरीद मैनुअल के अनुसार, मूल्य भिन्नता खंड (Price Variation Clause - PVC) आमतौर पर 18 महीने से अधिक अवधि वाले दीर्घकालिक अनुबंधों में शामिल किया जाता है ताकि कच्चे माल, श्रम मजदूरी आदि की बाजार दरों में उतार-चढ़ाव को संतुलित किया जा सके। इस खंड की मुख्य विशेषताएं हैं: (i) यह दोनों दिशाओं में काम करता है—सूचकांक बढ़ने पर मूल्य वृद्धि और सूचकांक घटने पर मूल्य में कटौती होती है, (ii) इसका सटीक गणितीय सूत्र और अधिकतम सीमा (Price Ceiling) निविदा प्रपत्र में पहले से निर्दिष्ट होनी चाहिए, तथा (iii) यह आधिकारिक मान्यता प्राप्त सूचकांकों (जैसे RBI/WPI/CPI सूचकांक) पर आधारित होता है। कोई भी विक्रेता बिना आधिकारिक दस्तावेजी प्रमाण और पूर्व-निर्धारित सूत्र के एकतरफा मूल्य वृद्धि की मांग कभी नहीं कर सकता। अतः कथन D गलत (INCORRECT) है और यही सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) It allows vendor to unilaterally demand higher price without documentary evidence.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: higher price without documentary evidence. A price variation clause adjusts contract prices based on documented variations in market indices for labor or material costs during long- term contracts. However, it never permits vendors to demand higher prices unilaterally without documentary evidence. Adjustments must follow explicit mathematical formulas and verifiable market indices specified in the original tender documents.

questions.explanation_english: Handling audit objections during an inspection follows a strictly structured procedure: First, the inspecting auditor identifies a discrepancy or requires clarification and issues an initial Audit Memo or Half-Margin Query (III). Second, the Principal/Head of Office examines the school records, compiles facts, prepares an official written reply supported by relevant vouchers or sanction files, and submits it to the audit party (I). Third, the audit team scrutinizes and reviews the submitted reply and supporting documentation (II). Fourth, if the explanation and evidence satisfactorily address the query in accordance with financial rules, the audit memo is dropped on the spot; if unsatisfactory or unresolved, it is converted into an audit paragraph and incorporated into the formal Inspection Report (IR) for departmental follow-up (IV). Thus, the correct sequence is III -> I -> II -> IV.
questions.explanation_hindi: निरीक्षण के दौरान ऑडिट आक्षेपों के समाधान की एक सुव्यवस्थित कालानुक्रमिक प्रक्रिया होती है: सबसे पहले, निरीक्षण लेखापरीक्षक किसी अनियमितता या विसंगति पर प्रारंभिक ऑडिट मेमो (Audit Memo/Query) जारी करता है (III)। इसके बाद, प्रधानाचार्य या कार्यालय प्रमुख अभिलेखों की जांच कर तथ्यों, वित्तीय स्वीकृतियों और साक्ष्यों के साथ लिखित उत्तर प्रस्तुत करते हैं (I)। तत्पश्चात, लेखापरीक्षा दल प्रस्तुत उत्तर और दस्तावेजों की समीक्षा व सत्यापन करता है (II)। अंत में, यदि उत्तर संतोषजनक और नियमों के अनुरूप पाया जाता है तो ऑडिट दल आपत्ति को वहीं समाप्त (Drop) कर देता है; अन्यथा असंतोषजनक रहने पर उसे अंतिम निरीक्षण रिपोर्ट (Inspection Report - IR) में औपचारिक पैराग्राफ के रूप में शामिल कर लिया जाता है (IV)। अतः सही क्रम III, I, II, IV है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) III, I, II, IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Handling audit objections follows a structured sequence. The auditor first issues an audit memo raising specific observations or queries. The establishment head submits a written reply with supporting evidence. The audit team evaluates the response and supporting documents. Satisfactory replies lead to dropping the paragraph; otherwise, it is included in the final report.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 238(1) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, Form GFR 12-A is the prescribed standard format for submitting Utilization Certificates (UC) in respect of non-recurring grants-in-aid sanctioned to autonomous bodies, grantee institutions, or local authorities. (Under the earlier GFR 2005 framework, Form GFR 19-A was used, which was updated to Form GFR 12-A in GFR 2017 for Autonomous Bodies and non-recurring grants, while Form GFR 12-C is used for other entities). Form GFR 12-A mandates grantee organizations to certify the total grants sanctioned, unspent balance brought forward, interest accrued on the grant funds, actual expenditure incurred on approved components, and unspent balance carried forward or surrendered. For educational administrators and school Principals managing government grants, adhering to Form GFR 12-A ensures statutory compliance and transparent accounting before requesting subsequent grant installments.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियमावली (GFR) 2017 के नियम 238(1) के अनुसार, स्वायत्त निकायों, अनुदानग्राही संस्थाओं या स्थानीय प्राधिकरणों को स्वीकृत अनावर्ती सहायता अनुदान (non-recurring grants-in-aid) के संबंध में उपयोगिता प्रमाण पत्र (UC) प्रस्तुत करने के लिए फॉर्म जीएफआर 12-ए (Form GFR 12-A) मानक निर्धारित प्रारूप है। (पूर्ववर्ती जीएफआर 2005 में इसके लिए फॉर्म जीएफआर 19-ए था, जिसे जीएफआर 2017 में संशोधित किया गया)। फॉर्म जीएफआर 12-ए में अनुदानग्राही संस्था को स्वीकृत कुल अनुदान, गत वर्ष की अव्ययित शेष राशि, अनुदान पर अर्जित ब्याज, स्वीकृत मदों पर किया गया वास्तविक व्यय तथा अभ्यर्पित अथवा आगे ले जाई गई शेष राशि को विधिवत प्रमाणित करना होता है। विद्यालय प्राचार्यों और वित्तीय प्रशासकों के लिए अनुदानों की अगली किस्त प्राप्त करने हेतु फॉर्म 12-ए में समय पर उपयोगिता प्रमाण पत्र प्रस्तुत करना कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य है।

questions.question_english: Which rule of GFR 2017 details the general principles governing contracts entered into by government authorities?

questions.explanation_english: Rule 225 of GFR 2017, situated in Chapter 8 ('Contract Management'), outlines the comprehensive general principles governing all contracts and agreements executed on behalf of the Government. These principles mandate that: (1) The terms of contract must be precise, definite, and leave no room for ambiguous interpretation; (2) Standard contract forms should be adopted wherever applicable; (3) Contracts must be executed on behalf of the President of India in conformity with Article 299(1) of the Constitution; (4) No contract involving uncertain or indefinite liability, or unusual conditions, should be finalized without prior concurrence of the Ministry of Finance; (5) Provisions for liquidated damages (LD), price variation clauses (PVC), warranty, and dispute resolution mechanisms must be clearly incorporated. (Rule 144 covers Fundamental Principles of Public Buying, Rule 194 governs Outsourcing of Services, and Rule 250 relates to Grants-in-aid).
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर (GFR) 2017 के अध्याय 8 ('अनुबंध प्रबंधन' / Contract Management) का नियम 225 सरकार की ओर से किए जाने वाले सभी अनुबंधों एवं समझौतों को नियंत्रित करने वाले मूलभूत सामान्य सिद्धांतों का विस्तृत विवरण प्रदान करता है। इन सिद्धांतों के अनुसार: (1) अनुबंध की शर्तें स्पष्ट, सुनिश्चित और असंदिग्ध होनी चाहिए; (2) जहां तक संभव हो, मानक अनुबंध प्रपत्रों (Standard Forms) का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए; (3) संविधान के अनुच्छेद 299(1) के अनुसार अनुबंध भारत के राष्ट्रपति के नाम पर निष्पादित होने चाहिए; (4) वित्त मंत्रालय की पूर्व सहमति के बिना अनिश्चित देनदारी या असामान्य शर्तों वाला कोई अनुबंध नहीं किया जाना चाहिए; (5) अनुबंध में देरी के लिए परिनिर्धारित हर्जाना (Liquidated Damages), मूल्य भिन्नता खंड तथा विवाद समाधान तंत्र का स्पष्ट उल्लेख होना चाहिए। (नियम 144 सार्वजनिक खरीद के सिद्धांतों से, नियम 194 सेवाओं की आउटसोर्सिंग से, और नियम 250 सहायता अनुदान से संबंधित है)।

It sets out basic legal requirements, contract conditions, standard forms, risk mitigation provisions, and price variation guidelines to safeguard public financial interests during contract execution.

questions.question_english: The fundamental principles of public buying under GFR 2017 mandate that every authority delegated with the financial powers of procuring goods in public interest shall have the responsibility and accountability to bring:
options_english: Profitability, flexibility, and speed
Centralization, standardization, and monopoly
Discretion, ambiguity, and bilateral negotiation
Efficiency, economy, and transparency
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 144 of GFR 2017, the opening mandate specifies:
"Every authority delegated with the financial powers of procuring goods in public interest shall have the responsibility and accountability to bring: (a) Efficiency, economy, and transparency; (b) Fair and equitable treatment of suppliers; and (c) Promotion of competition in public procurement."

Significance for School Principals:
When procuring classroom furniture, lab supplies, or smart boards, a Principal must:
1. Efficiency: Conduct procurement in a timely and organized manner without procedural delays.
2. Economy: Procure goods at the most competitive, reasonable market price.
3. Transparency: Maintain open specifications, objective criteria, and documented purchase files (preferably through GeM).
questions.explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के नियम 144 के तहत आरंभिक अधिदेश स्पष्ट रूप से निर्धारित करता है:
"सार्वजनिक हित में वस्तुओं की खरीद के लिए वित्तीय शक्तियों से संपन्न प्रत्येक प्राधिकारी की यह जिम्मेदारी और जवाबदेही होगी कि वह: (क) दक्षता, मितव्ययिता और पारदर्शिता; (ख) आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के साथ निष्पक्ष और न्यायसंगत व्यवहार; तथा (ग) सार्वजनिक खरीद में प्रतिस्पर्धा को बढ़ावा देना सुनिश्चित करे।"

विद्यालय प्राचार्यों के लिए महत्व:
कक्षा फर्नीचर, प्रयोगशाला आपूर्ति या स्मार्ट बोर्ड खरीदते समय प्राचार्य को निम्नलिखित सुनिश्चित करना चाहिए:
1. दक्षता (Efficiency): बिना प्रक्रियात्मक देरी के समयबद्ध खरीद करना।
2. मितव्ययिता (Economy): सबसे प्रतिस्पर्धी और उचित बाजार मूल्य पर सामान प्राप्त करना।
3. पारदर्शिता (Transparency): स्पष्ट विनिर्देश, वस्तुनिष्ठ मूल्यांकन मानदंड और पूर्ण दस्तावेज बनाए रखना (विशेषकर GeM के माध्यम से)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Efficiency, economy, and transparency

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Public procurement mandates that authorities exercising delegated financial powers bring efficiency, economy, and transparency to every transaction. Procuring officers are accountable for obtaining quality goods at competitive market rates while maintaining open, non- discriminatory procedures. Achieving optimal value for public money requires balancing swift administrative execution with robust anti- corruption mechanisms, equal opportunity for vendors, and thorough public documentation of choices.

questions.explanation_english: Rule 12 of GFR 2017 deals specifically with the 'General System of Financial Management and Control'. questions.question_english: At the close of the financial year on 31st March, how should the outstanding unspent balance in the permanent advance (imprest) register be accounted for if the establishment is closing the imprest account?
options_english: The unspent balance must be formally refunded and deposited into the Government Account.
It should be disbursed as a performance bonus among office staff members.
It should be transferred to the local Vidyalaya Kalyan Samiti (VKS) bank account.
It can be retained and carried forward as personal cash by the Head of Office.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 322 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 read with Rule 90 to 95 of the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983, a permanent advance (imprest) is granted to a Head of Office (HOO) or Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) to meet emergent, unforeseen, and petty contingent expenditures before drawing funds on regular bills. At the end of the financial year (31st March), if an office is closing its permanent advance or when directed by treasury/accounts authorities, all vouchers for expenditure incurred up to that date must be adjusted, and the remaining unspent physical cash balance must be formally refunded into the Consolidated Fund of India / Government Account via a military/civil treasury challan. Government financial discipline strictly prohibits retaining public money as private or personal cash, distributing public funds as unapproved staff bonuses, or irregularly diverting imprest money into non-governmental, local school management (e.g., VKS/SMC), or commercial bank accounts.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 322 तथा केंद्रीय सरकार खाता (प्राप्ति एवं भुगतान) नियम, 1983 के नियम 90 से 95 के अनुसार, कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) या आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को नियमित बिलों पर धनराशि आहरित करने से पूर्व आकस्मिक एवं तत्काल छोटे खर्चों को पूरा करने हेतु स्थायी अग्रिम (इम्प्रेस्ट) स्वीकृत किया जाता है। वित्तीय वर्ष की समाप्ति (31 मार्च) पर यदि कार्यालय द्वारा स्थायी अग्रिम को बंद किया जा रहा है या लेखा नियमों के तहत वर्ष के अंत में समायोजन अपेक्षित है, तो उस तिथि तक किए गए व्यय के सभी वाउचरों का विधिवत समायोजन किया जाना चाहिए तथा बची हुई अप्रयुक्त नकद राशि को चालान के माध्यम से सरकारी खाते (राजकोष) में अनिवार्य रूप से वापस जमा किया जाना चाहिए। वित्तीय नियमों के तहत सरकारी धनराशि को निजी नकदी के रूप में रखने, कर्मचारियों में बोनस के रूप में बांटने अथवा विद्यालय प्रबंधन/कल्याण समिति (VKS/SMC) जैसे स्थानीय बैंक खातों में अवैध रूप से अंतरित करने की सख्त मनाही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The unspent balance should be refunded to the Government Account.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: the Government Account. When an establishment closes its permanent advance or when required by specific accounting directions at year-end closure, any unspent cash balance must be formally refunded into the government account. Imprest funds cannot be retained as personal cash, disbursed as bonuses, or illegally transferred into non-governmental or local committee accounts.

questions.question_hindi: भंडार/सामग्री के कंडमनेशन (अनुपयोगी घोषित करने) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से सही कथन की पहचान कीजिए।
options_hindi: स्टॉक अभिरक्षा रखने वाला कोई भी अराजपत्रित समूह 'ग' (Group C) कर्मचारी स्वतंत्र रूप से कार्यालय की वस्तुओं को कंडम घोषित कर सकता है।
किसी वस्तु को कंडमनेशन समिति (Condemnation Committee) की सिफारिश पर ही अधिशेष, अप्रचलित या अनुपयोगी घोषित किया जा सकता है।
सरकारी परिसंपत्तियों के कंडमनेशन की प्रक्रिया बिना किसी भौतिक निरीक्षण के पूरी तरह से कागजी स्तर पर की जा सकती है।

questions.question_english: Identify the correct statement regarding the condemnation of stores and government assets under GFR 2017.
options_english: Any non-gazetted Group C employee holding stock custody can independently declare office items as condemned.
An item may be declared surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable on the recommendation of a duly constituted Condemnation Committee.
Condemnation of government assets can be processed entirely on paper without conducting any physical inspection.
Condemned items must be permanently stored in a dead stock room and must never be disposed of through public sale.
questions.explanation_english: According to Rule 217 and Rule 218 of GFR 2017, government stores cannot be arbitrarily declared condemned by individual storekeepers or stock custodians. The competent authority must constitute a Survey Committee / Condemnation Committee comprising competent officers (and technical experts where technical equipment is involved). This committee conducts a thorough physical inspection of the assets, evaluates repairability versus economic viability, and submits a formal condemnation report. Only upon the committee's formal recommendation and subsequent sanction by the competent authority under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) can goods be declared surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable for disposal.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियम 217 एवं 218 के अनुसार, किसी भी सरकारी भंडार या परिसंपत्ति को व्यक्तिगत स्टोरकीपर या लिपिक द्वारा मनमाने ढंग से अनुपयोगी घोषित नहीं किया जा सकता। सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा विधिवत गठित 'कंडमनेशन समिति' (Condemnation Committee / सर्वेक्षण समिति) द्वारा परिसंपत्तियों का भौतिक निरीक्षण किया जाता है। समिति उनकी उपयोगिता, मरम्मत की आर्थिक सार्थकता तथा तकनीकी अप्रचलन का मूल्यांकन करके अपनी औपचारिक संस्तुति प्रस्तुत करती है। सक्षम प्राधिकारी की वित्तीय स्वीकृति के उपरांत ही उन वस्तुओं को अधिशेष, अप्रचलित या अनुपयोगी घोषित कर निपटान की कार्रवाई की जाती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) An item may be declared surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable on recommendation of a Condemnation Committee.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: or unserviceable on recommendation of a Condemnation Committee. Condemnation of public property requires formal evaluation by a duly constituted Condemnation Committee or Board. The committee physically inspects the assets and submits formal recommendations regarding unserviceability, technical obsolescence, or surplus status. Individual storekeepers or Group C employees cannot independently declare assets condemned without proper committee inspection and competent authority sanction.

questions.question_english: Under the framework of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 and DFPR, how is a "Head of Office" officially declared?
options_english: Through a formal resolution adopted by the local municipal body.
By an automatic seniority-based order within a particular office establishment.
Through a statutory notification issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
By the Head of Department (HOD) issuing a formal administrative order under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR).
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 2 of GFR 2017 and Rule 3(f) of the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR), 1978, a 'Head of Office' means a Gazetted Officer declared as such by a Head of Department (HOD) under Rule 14 of DFPR. In schools, the Director of Education (who acts as HOD) formally declares the school Principal/Vice-Principal as the Head of Office (HOO), empowering them to exercise specified administrative and financial powers, sanction contingent expenditure, and operate official establishment accounts.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 2 और वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियम (DFPR), 1978 के नियम 3(f) तथा नियम 14 के अनुसार, 'कार्यालय प्रमुख' (Head of Office - HOO) उस राजपत्रित अधिकारी को घोषित किया जाता है जिसे विभागाध्यक्ष (Head of Department - HOD) द्वारा एक औपचारिक लिखित आदेश द्वारा ऐसा घोषित किया गया हो। उदाहरण के लिए, शिक्षा निदेशालय में शिक्षा निदेशक (विभागाध्यक्ष) द्वारा स्कूल के प्रधानाचार्य (Principal) को कार्यालय प्रमुख घोषित किया जाता है, जिससे उन्हें दैनिक आकस्मिक व्यय स्वीकृत करने तथा प्रशासनिक शक्तियां प्रयोग करने का अधिकार प्राप्त होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) By the Head of Department through a formal order under DFPR.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: formal order under DFPR. A Head of Office is formally declared by the competent Head of Department issuing a specific administrative order under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules. This declaration grants designated administrative and financial responsibilities to a gazetted officer, enabling them to manage day-to-day office expenditure, authorize routine administrative bills, maintain official accounts, and manage local establishment matters for that specific government unit.
